claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To start, could you please tell me how many children you're enquiring about, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! Thank you for reaching out. It's lovely to meet you, and I'm happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

To continue, could you tell me: are you responsible for Alex's care? For example, does he live with you, and are you the person who looks after him day-to-day?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, no actually - Alex doesn't live with me. He lives with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex lives with his mum and she is responsible for his day-to-day care, she would typically be the one eligible to claim Child Benefit for him, rather than yourself.

Just to confirm a couple more things:

Do you contribute financially towards Alex's upkeep, for example by paying maintenance? And is Alex's mum already claiming Child Benefit for him, to your knowledge?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I don't contribute anything financially at the moment, no. And yes, his mum is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being so honest and clear about the situation.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex lives with his mum, not with you
- You are not responsible for his day-to-day care
- You do not contribute financially towards his upkeep
- His mum is already claiming Child Benefit for him

I now have enough information to make a decision on your eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**For Alex:**
To be eligible for Child Benefit, you must be "responsible" for the child. This usually means either:
- The child lives with you, or
- You're contributing towards the cost of the child's upkeep

In your case:
- Alex doesn't live with you — he lives with his mum
- You're not responsible for his day-to-day care
- You don't contribute financially towards his upkeep
- His mum is already claiming Child Benefit for him

Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at any one time, and since Alex's mum is responsible for his care and is already receiving the benefit, she is the rightful claimant.

I hope this helps clarify things. If your circumstances change in the future (for example, if Alex comes to live with you), you may become eligible at that point. Is there anything else I can help you with?
